title: Constant realization reflects derived isomorphisms and perfectness on a nondegenerate site
statement: Let $C$ be a site with object universe $u$, morphism universe $v$, Grothendieck topology $J$, and the usual abelian-group and ring sheafifications on $C$ and its slices [def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor]. Let $R$ be a commutative ring in universe $\max(u,v)$ and choose independent derived-localization universes for modules, module sheaves and restricted module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. If the empty sieve does not cover $U$, exact constant realization followed by restriction to $U$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction] reflects isomorphisms of arbitrary algebraic derived complexes. If $J$ comes from a precoverage satisfying the covering axioms [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], has a terminal object not covered by the empty sieve, and the constant realizations of $P$ and $L$ are isomorphic with $P$ perfect [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], then $L$ is perfect.

source.place: Tag 09C5, first proof paragraph: perfectness of the algebraic residue marking. Constant realization and local maps: Tags 093J, 00WB, 00WK and 09BE; derived homology criterion Tags 05RU and 05RT.

proof.text: The module sheafification unit is injective on an object not covered by the empty sieve. Equality of two constant sections gives a covering equalizer sieve. If the constants differ, that sieve is empty. In particular a constant module whose restriction is zero must be zero.

The constant-module functor [def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor] and restriction [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction] are exact, so their derived functors commute with homology. If the realized restricted map is invertible, its cohomology kernels and cokernels realize to zero and therefore vanish by the preceding step. Every algebraic cohomology map is invertible, so the derived map is invertible.

Apply [lem-sfb-perfect-constant-derived-map-local] to the isomorphism from the perfect constant realization. At least one member of its covering is not covered by the empty sieve, since otherwise transitivity would make that sieve cover the terminal object. The local algebraic map realizes an isomorphism there, hence is invertible by the preceding step. Transport the bounded finite-projective representative to conclude that L is perfect.
